title: Safety Codes Council Fire Sub-Council tribunal: Council Order No. 2025-07 on shingle pile size and classification (City of Calgary order)
jurisdiction: Calgary, Alberta (City order under the Safety Codes Act; Fire Sub-Council Administrative Tribunal)
code_edition: unknown if unstated (decision names the Fire Code and NFPA 13 without an edition year)

facts.text: The City of Calgary issued an order dated 17 July 2025 about the size of shingle piles at a Calgary property. The appeal was heard virtually.
facts.locator: p.1 preamble and para 1; p.2 para 7 (record item 2)

facts.text: The record lists the Notice of Appeal (18 Aug 2025), the City Order (17 Jul 2025), and both parties' briefs (10 Nov 2025).
The issue is the classification of post-consumer shingles under NFPA 13 and the resulting limits on pile size and height.
The appellant argued the City treated the 35-day appeal period as a compliance timeline and did not weigh scale, machinery, labour and disposal constraints.
The appellant argued post-consumer asphalt roofing shingles are not Class III or Class IV commodities under the Fire Code, and that the City relied on explanatory material and Annex A of NFPA 13.

The tribunal's powers under subsection 52(2) of the Safety Codes Act include varying the order and, as a term of its order, issuing a written variance where it provides approximately equivalent or greater safety performance.
The tribunal found the City authorised to issue the order to the individual who held himself out as owner and operator.

The tribunal stated that the Fire Code adopts NFPA 13's commodity classification framework for outdoor storage and that the Annex tables list roofing shingles as Class III and Class IV. It rejected the appellant's narrowing of those classes to new pallet-packed shingles.
The tribunal accepted that the order had administrative deficiencies but held they did not justify revoking it.
The order was varied: one named individual was removed as a party, the order was issued to two numbered Alberta companies, and the compliance date was amended to 1 June 2026.

The decision is signed by the Chair, Fire Sub-Council Administrative Tribunal, on 26 January 2026. The signature block reads 'Signed at the City of Edmonton' although the matter concerns Calgary property.
